macro_blurb: Today's tape is dominated by a structural shift in tech: SpaceX has filed for an IPO that could vault Elon Musk to trillionaire status, even as its prospectus discloses billion-dollar losses, while Jim Cramer argues the tech investing playbook has permanently changed. Software pressure is visible at Intuit, which announced a roughly 17% workforce cut citing slowing growth, and Jeff Bezos used a CNBC interview to defend billionaires, talk taxes, and tout AI — keeping the mega-cap AI narrative front and center for US equities. On the EU side, the UK sealed a £3.7bn trade deal with six Gulf states, a modest positive for UK-listed exporters and broader European trade sentiment. A sinkhole-driven runway closure at LaGuardia is adding operational friction for US airlines.
synthesis:
Today's screen is a pure US value-and-momentum print: 10 of 10 picks are US-listed, average Value sits at the 85.8th percentile and Momentum at 82.4, while Quality lags at 62.8 and Yield at 65.6. The composite range is tight (74.1–85.3), and the sector mix is unusually flat — eight sectors represented, no concentration above two names. What unites the book is multiple compression: HPQ at 8x earnings vs Tech median 35x, EG at 7.3x vs 16.5x, ALL at 4.9x vs 16.5x, CNC and DVA both screening top-decile on FCF yield. This is a deep-value tape with momentum confirming, not a quality screen.

Three threads carry the list. First, the cash-return trade: HPQ (5.72% dividend, 14.6% FCF yield), MO (5.73%, 7%), BBY (6.48%) and ALL (21.8% FCF yield, $4bn buyback) cluster on shareholder yield while Bezos and Cramer keep the AI-capex narrative pulling mega-cap flows elsewhere. Second, the cheap-and-running cyclicals — CF (+29% 3M), APA (+37%), DVA (+30%), CNC (+34%) — all top-decile momentum on single-digit-to-mid-teens multiples. Third, leverage is doing real work: APA at 61, BBY at 139, DVA at 1,261 debt/equity. The discounts are not free.

The outlier is EG — a Financial Services name carried by Value (98th percentile) with only middling momentum (65) and a sub-sector ROE. The conspicuous absence is Technology: 1 of 10 despite the AI tape dominating headlines, and Industrials, Utilities and Communication Services are missing entirely from 992 screened names — a screen this US-concentrated and Tech-light is itself a concentration risk. Watch HPQ's Q2 print against the Alphabet/Gemini-in-PCs overhang, and any oil rollover that would expose APA's leverage in the next two weeks.
